newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up 1.44 pct in rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up 1.44 pct in rebound.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Monday in a technical rebound after five straight sessions of falls, brokers said.
The index ended up 119.62 points or 1.44 percent at 8,421.87. Turnover was an active T$99.4 billion, about half of the level in early April when the market rallied.
Constructions led the rebound, rising 4.06 percent on a local newspaper report that the Finance Ministry was considering relaxing rules on banks' investment in the property market.
Officials declined to confirm the report.
Hung Fu Constructions surged T$3 to T$46.3.

The paper said the ministry plans to revise the Banking Law to allow banks to invest in properties they do not occupy and set a ceiling for such investment at 40 percent of each bank's net asset value.
Currently, the law only allows banks to purchase properties for their own use.
"Allowing banks to have more flexible operations is an inevitable trend and the construction sector should benefit most from this reported move," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
Plastics were also strong, rising 3.15 percent, reflecting reports that Formosa Plastics group may build a petrochemical complex in Australia.
Formosa officials declined to comment on the report.
Formosa Plastics rose T$2 to T$70.
"Investors are simply using these reports to launch a technical rebound, but the slower turnover indicates investors are still very cautious," said HSBC James Capel senior analyst Alex Chen.
"The government's recent move to cool off the market is clear, so the rebound won't be too strong. The index should consolidate between 8,200-8,600 in the near term," Chen said.
Both the central bank and the Securities and Exchange Commssion have issued warnings in recent stock market rallies, which had once risen 25 percent in 1997 alone.

Textiles rose 2.90 percent, while electronics, which had suffered the heaviest profit-taking in recent sessions, rebounded 1.43 percent, with chipmaker United Microelectronics up T$1 to T$63.5. -- James Peng (5080815)
